senses.gloss: श्लि = √ श्रि, in प्र-शित, q.v.
श्लिकु m. (accord. to Uṇ. i, 33 fr. √ 2. श्लिष्) a servant, slave, dependant, L.
a profligate or low person, L.
श्लिकु m. n. astronomy, astrology, L.
श्लिकु f. n. exhaustion, L.
1. श्लिष् (cf. √ 1. श्रिष्) cl. 1. P. श्लेषति, to burn, Dhātup. xvii, 52.
श्लिषा f. clinging, embracing, L.
श्लिष्ट mfn. clinging or adhering to (loc. or comp.), Kāṭh.; KātyŚr.; MBh. &c.
(with सर्वतः) adhering closely, fitting tight (as a coat of mail), MBh. vii, 5161
adhering to one's self i.e. not affecting others, merely personal (as an art or science), Mālav. i, 15 (v.l. शिष्ट)
joined together, united, connected, MBh.; Kāv. &c.
clasped, embraced, Kāv.; Kathās.
(in rhet.) connected so as to be susceptible of a double interpretation, equivocal, Sāh.
श्लिष्ट—परम्परित-रूपक n. a continuous series of words having a double meaning (a kind of metaphor), Śiś., Sch.
श्लिष्ट—रूपक n. ambiguity as a metaphor, Kāv. ii, 87.
श्लिष्ट—वर्त्मन् n. the adhering together of the eyelids, ŚārṅgS.
श्लिष्टाक्षेप m. an objection expressed through using words containing a double meaning, Kāvyād. ii, 159; 160.
श्लिष्टार्थ-दीपक n. a Dīpaka (q.v.) containing a double meaning, ib. ii, 113; 114.
श्लिष्टोक्ति f. an expression containing a d˚ m˚, Kathās.
श्लिष्टि f. adherence, connection, MW.
an embrace, ib.
श्लिष्टि m. N. of a son of Dhruva, Hariv.; VP.
श्ली-पद n. (thought by some to be fr. √ श्लिष् + पद; others suppose श्ली to have the meaning ‘elephant’) morbid enlargement of the leg, swelled leg, elephantiasis, Suśr.; Bhpr. &c.
श्ली-पद—प्रभव m. ‘source of elephantiasis’, the Mango tree, L.
श्लीपदापह m. ‘removing or curing elephantiasis’, the tree Putranjiva Roxburghii, L.
श्लीपदिन् mfn. having a swelled leg, suffering from elephantiasis
श्लीपदिन् m. a club-footed man, Mn. iii, 165
श्लील mfn. (= श्रीर; cf. अ-श्लील) prosperous, fortunate, affluent, happy, W.
